title: Ensure 'Logon Password' is set
description: Changes the default login password. The login password is used for SSH connections. The default device configuration does not require any strong user authentication enabling unfettered access to an attacker that can reach the device. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal pager 0' first; 'more system:running-config' also works and shows unmasked secrets).
reference: CIS Cisco ASA 9.x Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.1.1 Ensure 'Logon Password' is set

remediation.command:
! Run the following to set the login password.
passwd <login_password> The login_password parameter should be the plain-text password used to log into the system

title: Ensure 'Enable Password' is set
description: Sets the password for users accessing privileged EXEC mode when they run the enable command. The default device configuration does not require any strong user authentication enabling unfettered access to an attacker that can reach the device. A user can enter the default password and just press the Enter key at the Password prompt to login to the ... Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal pager 0' first; 'more system:running-config' also works and shows unmasked secrets).
reference: CIS Cisco ASA 9.x Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.1.2 Ensure 'Enable Password' is set

remediation.command:
! Run the following to set the enable password.
enable password <enable_password> level <privilege_level> The enable_password parameter should be the plain-text password used to log into the enable mode If the privilege level is not configured, the default one is 15

title: Ensure 'Password Recovery' is disabled
description: Disables the password recovery. Disabling the password recovery is an additional physical control. It will prevent an attacker that will have circumvented all the physical safeguards and being in contact with the security appliance to change the existing login password, enable password and ... Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal pager 0' first; 'more system:running-config' also works and shows unmasked secrets).
reference: CIS Cisco ASA 9.x Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.1.4 Ensure 'Password Recovery' is disabled

remediation.command:
! Run the following to disable the password recovery:
no service password-recovery

title: Ensure 'Password Policy' is enabled
description: Enforces the Enterprise Password Policy by setting compliant local password requirements for the security appliance. The password policy helps to prevent unauthorized accesses by enforcing the password for more complexity and making them difficult to be guessed. This applies to the local database. Fails unless minimum-length (>= 14), uppercase, lowercase, numeric and special minimums are configured; also fails on lifetime > 365 (or 0) and minimum-changes < 14 when set. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal pager 0' first; 'more system:running-config' also works and shows unmasked secrets).
reference: CIS Cisco ASA 9.x Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.1.5 Ensure 'Password Policy' is enabled

remediation.command:
! - Step 1: Run the following to set the password lifetime in days to less than or equal to 365
password-policy lifetime 365
- Step 2: Run the following to set the minimum number of characters that must be changed between the old and the new passwords, to be to be greater than or equal to 14
password-policy minimum-changes 14
- Step 3: Run the following to set the minimum number of upper case characters in the password, to be to be greater than or equal to 1
password-policy minimum-uppercase 1
- Step 4: Run the following to set the minimum number of lower case characters in the password, to be to be greater than or equal to 1
password-policy minimum-lowercase 1
- Step 5: Run the following to set the minimum number of numeric characters in the password, to be greater than or equal to 1
password-policy minimum-numeric 1
- Step 6: Run the following to set the minimum number of special characters in the password, to be greater than or equal to 1
password-policy minimum-special 1
- Step 7: Run the following to set the password minimum length, to be greater than or equal to 14
password-policy minimum-length 14

title: Ensure 'aaa local authentication max failed attempts' is set to less than or equal to '3'
description: Limits the maximum number of times a local user can enter a wrong password before being locked out. Limiting the number of failed authentication attempts is a prevention and safeguard against brute force and dictionary attacks on systems. The implementation of the aaa local authentication max failed attempts helps to limit the number of consecutive failed ... Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal pager 0' first; 'more system:running-config' also works and shows unmasked secrets).
reference: CIS Cisco ASA 9.x Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.4.1.1 Ensure 'aaa local authentication max failed attempts' is set to less than or equal to '3'

remediation.command:
! Run the following to configure the maximum number of consecutive local login failures to be less than or equal to 3
aaa local authentication attempts max-fail 3

title: Ensure known default accounts do not exist
description: Deletes the known default accounts configured. In order to attempt access to known devices' platforms, attackers use the available database of the known default accounts for each platform or Operating System. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal pager 0' first; 'more system:running-config' also works and shows unmasked secrets).
reference: CIS Cisco ASA 9.x Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.4.1.3 Ensure known default accounts do not exist

title: Ensure 'TACACS+/RADIUS' is configured correctly
description: Specifies the AAA server-group and each individual server using the TACACS+ or RADIUS protocol. Authentication, authorization and accounting (AAA) scheme provide an authoritative source for managing and monitoring access for devices. Many protocols are supported for the communication between the systems and the AAA servers: http-form, kerberos, ldap, ... Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal pager 0' first; 'more system:running-config' also works and shows unmasked secrets).

remediation.command:
! - Step 1: Acquire the enterprise standard protocol (protocol_name) for authentication (TACACS+ or RADIUS)
- Step 2: Run the following to configure the AAA server-group for the required protocol
aaa-server <server-group_name> protocol <protocol_name>
- Step 3: Run the following to configure the AAA server:
aaa-server <server-group_name> (<interface_name>) host <aaa-server_ip> <shared_key> server-group_name: the above server-group configured interface_name: the network interface from which the AAA server will be accessed aaa-server_ip: the IP address of the AAA server shared_key: the TACACS+ or RADIUS shared key

title: Ensure 'aaa authentication http console' is configured correctly
description: Authenticates ASDM users who access the security appliance over HTTP. By default, the enable password is used in combination with no username for http access. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal pager 0' first; 'more system:running-config' also works and shows unmasked secrets).

title: Ensure 'aaa authentication ssh console' is configured correctly
description: Authenticates users who access the device using SSH. Using AAA authentication for interactive management access to the device provides consistent, centralized control of your network. title: Ensure 'aaa command authorization' is configured correctly
description: Defines the source of authorization for the commands entered by an administrator/user. Requiring authorization for commands enforces separation of duties and provides least privilege access for specific job roles. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal pager 0' first; 'more system:running-config' also works and shows unmasked secrets).

description: Limits the access to the privileged EXEC mode. When a user is placed in the privileged EXEC mode, valuable information can be obtained. When authentication is not enabled, attackers can disguise as NTP servers and broadcast wrong time and it will be difficult to correlate events upon an incident. In some other cases, attackers can perform NTP DDoS attacks such as NTP Amplification. title: Ensure 'OSPF authentication' is enabled
description: Enables the authentication of OSPF neighbor before routing information is received from the neighbor. Enabling the routing protocol authentication prevents against attackers who can send wrong routing information in order to redirect traffic to their network or send malformed packets in order to saturate and to exhaust the control plane. Not applicable (passes) when no 'router ospf' is configured; otherwise fails if no interface has OSPF MD5 authentication. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal pager 0' first; 'more system:running-config' also works and shows unmasked secrets).

title: Ensure ICMP is restricted for untrusted interfaces
description: Allows ICMP traffic for specific hosts or subnets and denies ICMP traffic for all other sources. ICMP is an important troubleshooting tool that can also be used to perform ICMP attacks on untrusted interfaces. For these interfaces, the ICMP traffic should be allowed only for specific hosts or subnets that are trusted by the Enterprise and should be ... - Step 2: Run the following command to deny fragments on the interface.

title: Ensure VPN traffic goes through the relevant ACL
description: By default, the traffic going through IPSEC tunnel (policy-based) bypasses the ACL of the interface the VPN terminates on, often the outside ACL. VPN are used to interconnect sites, whether intra or inter companies. In many cases, these are seen to extensions of the local network and very little filtering is applied. CIS marks this Manual; automated because the non-default 'no sysopt connection permit-vpn' line is visible in the config. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal pager 0' first; 'more system:running-config' also works and shows unmasked secrets).
reference: CIS Cisco ASA 9.x Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.13 Ensure VPN traffic goes through the relevant ACL

remediation.command:
Summary
- Step 1: determine on which interface(s) the IPSEC tunnel ends
- Step 2: determine the ACL applied to the interface
- Step 3: add an ACE to the ACL to permit the traffic temporarily
- Step 4: disable the bypass
Step 1
show run full | grep crypto.map..*.interface. crypto map my_remote_sites interface outside In this example, the crypto map my_remote_sites is applied to the interface outside: the IPSEC tunnel terminates on the interface outside.
Step 2
sh run access-group | grep interface.outside access-group outside_acl in interface outside The ACL outside_acl is applied to the interface outside.

audit.command: CIS assessment: Manual. Step 1: Run the following to determine whether the protocol <protocol_name> to be inspected is included in the default policy hostname#sh run policy-map | in __inspect.<protocol_name> The output should look like: inspect protocol_name The example below confirms that the FTP protocol is inspected Asa# sh run policy-map | in __inspect.ftp inspect ftp - Step 2: If an output is displayed, the system is compliant. remediation.command:

title: Ensure DOS protection is enabled for untrusted interfaces
description: Determines the maximum connections, maximum embryonic connections, maximum connections per client and maximum embryonic connections per client that can be accepted on the outside interface. Limiting the number of connections protects from a DoS attack. The ASA uses the per-client limits and the embryonic connection limits to trigger TCP Intercept, which protects inside systems from a DoS attack perpetrated by flooding an interface with TCP SYN ... CIS assessment: Manual. Reported as SKIP with review instructions.
reference: CIS Cisco ASA 9.x Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.5 Ensure DOS protection is enabled for untrusted interfaces

audit.command: CIS assessment: Manual. - Step 1: Run the following to determine whether the DOS protection is enabled hostname#sh run policy-map | i set.connection The output should look like: set connection connection_type max_value The example below gives the values for maximum connections, maximum embryonic connections, maximum connections per client and maximum embryonic connections per client Asa#sh run policy-map | i set.connection set connection conn-max 9500 set connection embryonic-conn-max 5000 set connection per-client-embryonic-max 100 set connection ...

remediation.command:
! - Step 1: Acquire the enterprise standard values for maximum connections, maximum embryonic connections, maximum connections per client and maximum embryonic connections per client
- Step 2: Run the following to configure the class to identify the traffic on which DOS protection should be performed.
class-map <class_name>
match any
Step 3: Run the following to configure the policy that will determine the maximum connections to be applied on the class previously configured
policy-map <policy_name>
class <class_name>
set connection conn-max <enterprise_max_number>
set connection embryonic-conn-max <enterprise_max_number>
set connection per-client-embryonic-max <enterprise_max_number>
set connection per-client-max <enterprise_max_number> The enterprise_max_number parameter is to be taken between 0 and 65535.
- Step 4: Run the following to apply the policy previously configured on the untrusted
service-policy <policy_name> interface <untrusted_interface_name>

description: Enables the unicast Reverse-Path Forwarding (uRPF) on untrusted interfaces. description: Sets the security level of the Internet facing interface to 0. Where security zones are not configured, the Internet facing interface is the most untrusted interface and must have the lowest security-level that is 0. Therefore, any traffic initiated from this interface to the other interfaces of the security appliance ... Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal pager 0' first; 'more system:running-config' also works and shows unmasked secrets).

title: Ensure Botnet protection is enabled for untrusted interfaces
description: Filters Botnet traffic on the untrusted interface. In a Botnet condition, many computers in the Enterprise network after being infected with malware and mostly trojans will collect data without the knowledge of the users owning them and send it to the attacker network. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal pager 0' first; 'more system:running-config' also works and shows unmasked secrets).
reference: CIS Cisco ASA 9.x Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.9 Ensure Botnet protection is enabled for untrusted interfaces

remediation.command:
! - Step 1: Run the following command to ensure that the DNS server is available.
sh run | i name-server If there is no DNS server, configure the DNS server according to the related recommendation.
- Step 2: Run the following commands to enable the security appliance to download and use for inspection the lists of known malware websites
dynamic-filter updater-client enable
dynamic-filter use-database
- Step 3: Run the following command to create a class map for the security appliance to match the DNS traffic
class-map <dns_class_map_name>
match port udp eq domain
- Step 4: Run the following to create the policy-map in order to ask the appliance to inspect the matched DNS traffic and to compare the domain name in the DNS traffic with the list of known malware related domain names.
policy-map <dns_policy_map_name>
class <dns_class_map_name>
inspect dns preset_dns_map dynamic-filter-snoop
- Step 5: Run the following for the inspection to be applied on the untrusted interface
service-policy <dns_policy_map_name> interface <untrusted_interface_name>
- Step 6: Run the following to monitor the Botnet traffic crossing the untrusted interface
dynamic-filter enable interface <untrusted_interface_name>
- Step 7: Run the following to drop any identified Botnet traffic on the untrusted interface
dynamic-filter drop blacklist interface <untrusted_interface_name>

title: Ensure ActiveX filtering is enabled
description: Removes ActiveX controls from the HTTP reply traffic received on the security appliance. ActiveX controls are used to provide a rich users' browsing experience. Because the ActiveX control is a written program that is executed in the users' computers, it can be used by attackers to perform malicious tasks on the machines of their victims. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal pager 0' first; 'more system:running-config' also works and shows unmasked secrets).

remediation.command:
! - Step 1: Acquire the TCP port used for the HTTP traffic containing ActiveX objects, the IP address <internal_users_ip> and mask <internal_users_mask> of internal users generating the HTTP traffic, and the IP address <external_servers_ip> and mask <external_servers_mask> of the external servers to which the internal users connect and that are source of ActiveX objects.
- Step 2: Run the following command to filter ActiveX applets.
filter activex <port> <internal_users_ip> <internal_users_mask> <external_servers_ip> <external_servers_mask>

Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal pager 0' first; 'more system:running-config' also works and shows unmasked secrets).

filter java <port> <internal_users_ip> <internal_users_mask> <external_servers_ip> <external_servers_mask>

Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal pager 0' first; 'more system:running-config' also works and shows unmasked secrets).

! - Step 1: Acquire the name <access-list_name> of the access-list that is not compliant from the audit procedure
